title: Gnocchi in Turmeric Yoghurt Sauce
subtitle: with baked potato gnocchi and fresh tomato
description: Light homemade potato gnocchi made from salt-baked potatoes, tossed in a turmeric butter and cream sauce with yoghurt, then finished with fresh tomato and za'atar.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220°C and line a tray with baking paper. Spread the coarse salt in an even layer on the tray, place the unpeeled potatoes on top and bake for about 1 hour until soft.
While still hot, halve the potatoes with a serrated knife and scoop out the flesh with a spoon.

Mash the potato flesh with a fork until smooth and lump-free. Add salt and the parmesan, mix briefly, then sprinkle over the flour and egg and mix with a fork. Quickly and briefly mix with your fingers, adjusting the flour gradually as needed to get a soft but slightly dry dough that is easy to work and not sticky. Do not overwork it.

Divide the dough into 5 equal balls and flatten slightly on a floured surface. Roll each into a long rope a little over 1 cm thick, cut into 1.5 cm pieces and arrange on a tray lined with semolina or flour.

Prepare a bowl of iced water and bring plenty of salted water to the boil in a large pot. Cook the gnocchi in batches for about 1 minute, just until they float. Remove with a slotted spoon to the iced water, then transfer to a container and toss with a little olive oil. They keep in the fridge for about 3 days.

Make the sauce: heat the butter, thinly sliced garlic and turmeric in a wide pan until the butter melts and for another half minute. Add the cream, stir and let it bubble for a few seconds. Add the cooked gnocchi and toss to heat through (add a spoon of water if needed). Remove from the heat, add the yoghurt, stir gently and season with a little salt.
Transfer to a serving plate, squeeze the tomato half over the top, sprinkle with za'atar and drizzle with olive oil.
